title: SSC CGL — General Awareness | Indian Polity
description: Subject-wise test on Indian Polity (General Awareness) for SSC CGL. 30Q.
subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Rights?

options.explanation: Part II deals with Citizenship
Part III enumerates the Fundamental Rights
Part IV deals with Directive Principles of State Policy
Part V deals with The Union

questions.explanation: Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12-35) enumerates the Fundamental Rights, which are justiciable rights essential for the all-round development of individuals.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: The concept of 'Judicial Review' in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from which country's constitution?

options.explanation: Judicial Review was not borrowed from the UK constitution
Judicial Review was borrowed from the US constitution
Judicial Review was not borrowed from the Canadian constitution
Judicial Review was not borrowed from the Australian constitution

questions.explanation: The concept of Judicial Review, which allows the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders, is a significant feature borrowed from the Constitution of the United States of America.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President of India declare a financial emergency?

options.explanation: Article 352 deals with National Emergency
Article 356 deals with State Emergency (President's Rule)
Article 360 empowers the President to declare a financial emergency
Article 365 is not related to financial emergency

questions.explanation: Article 360 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to declare a financial emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Which of the following statements about a 'Money Bill' in India is correct?

options.text: It can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
options.explanation: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha

options.text: It requires the prior recommendation of the President for introduction.
options.explanation: A Money Bill requires the prior recommendation of the President

options.text: The Rajya Sabha has the power to reject a Money Bill.
options.explanation: The Rajya Sabha cannot reject a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations

options.text: It is defined in Article 109 of the Constitution.
options.explanation: A Money Bill is defined in Article 110 of the Constitution

questions.explanation: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and requires the prior recommendation of the President.

questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, is related to which of the following?

options.explanation: The 73rd Amendment is not related to Fundamental Duties
The 73rd Amendment is related to Panchayati Raj Institutions
The 73rd Amendment is not related to Goods and Services Tax
The 73rd Amendment is related to Panchayati Raj Institutions

questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, is related to Panchayati Raj Institutions.

questions.question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Fundamental Rights?

options.explanation: Part II deals with the citizenship of India.
Part III enshrines the Fundamental Rights.
Part IV deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy.
Part V deals with the Union.

questions.explanation: Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution enshrines the Fundamental Rights, guaranteeing various civil liberties to all citizens.

questions.question: What is the minimum age required for a person to be elected as a member of the Lok Sabha?

options.explanation: This is the minimum age for voting.
This is the minimum age for being a candidate for some other offices.
This is the minimum age for being a member of the Lok Sabha.
This is not the minimum age for being a member of the Lok Sabha.

questions.explanation: Article 84(b) of the Indian Constitution states that a person shall not be less than 25 years of age to be qualified to be chosen to fill a seat in the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: The concept of 'Judicial Review' in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the constitution of which of the following countries?

options.explanation: The concept of Judicial Review in the Indian Constitution is not borrowed from the UK.
The concept of Judicial Review in the Indian Constitution is not borrowed from Canada.
The concept of Judicial Review in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the USA.
The concept of Judicial Review in the Indian Constitution is not borrowed from Australia.

questions.explanation: The concept of Judicial Review, which allows the judiciary to review legislative enactments and executive orders, is largely inspired by the Constitution of the United States of America.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions in India?

options.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act did not give constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions.
The 73rd Amendment Act gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions.
The 74th Amendment Act dealt with the municipalities.
The 61st Amendment Act did not give constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions.

questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 provided constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions, adding Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution, dealing with their structure, powers, and functions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty as enshrined in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions.
options.explanation: This is a Fundamental Duty.

options.text: To protect and improve the natural environment.
options.explanation: This is a Fundamental Duty.
Voting is not explicitly listed as a Fundamental Duty.

options.text: To safeguard public property and abjure violence.
options.explanation: This is a Fundamental Duty.

questions.explanation: While voting is an important civic responsibility in a democracy, it is not explicitly listed as a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution. The other options are indeed Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: Article 17 of the Indian Constitution deals with the abolition of which of the following?

options.explanation: Article 18 deals with the abolition of titles.
Article 17 abolishes 'Untouchability'.
Child Labour is not abolished by Article 17.
Forced Labour is dealt with in Article 23.

questions.explanation: Article 17 of the Indian Constitution abolishes 'Untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form. The enforcement of any disability arising out of 'Untouchability' shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the President of India: I. The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha on the advice of the Prime Minister. II. The President appoints the Chief Justice of India and other judges of the Supreme Court. III. The President can declare a national emergency if he/she is satisfied that a grave emergency exists, without the need for a written recommendation from the Union Cabinet. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.explanation: Statement III is incorrect.
Statement III is incorrect.
Statements I and II are correct.
Statement III is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct (Article 85(2)(b)). Statement II is correct (Article 124(2)). Statement III is incorrect because, after the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, the President can declare a national emergency only on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet (Article 352(3)).
questions.subject: ssc-gk

questions.question: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to the states and union territories?

options.explanation: The Third Schedule deals with the oaths and affirmations.
The Fourth Schedule deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha.
The Fifth Schedule deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
The Sixth Schedule deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in certain states.

questions.explanation: The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) to the states and union territories based on their population.

questions.question: The 'Doctrine of Basic Structure' of the Indian Constitution, which limits the Parliament's power to amend the Constitution, was propounded by the Supreme Court in which landmark case?

options.explanation: The Golaknath case is related to the amendment of the Constitution, but it did not propound the 'Doctrine of Basic Structure'.

options.text: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
options.explanation: The S.R. Bommai case is related to the imposition of President's Rule, but it did not propound the 'Doctrine of Basic Structure'.

options.text: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
options.explanation: The Kesavananda Bharati case propounded the 'Doctrine of Basic Structure'.

options.text: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
options.explanation: The Minerva Mills case is related to the amendment of the Constitution, but it did not propound the 'Doctrine of Basic Structure'.

questions.explanation: The 'Doctrine of Basic Structure' was laid down by the Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala case in 1973, holding that while Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution, it cannot alter its basic structure.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of Article and its subject is correctly matched?

options.explanation: Article 19 deals with the protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.

options.text: Article 21: Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression
options.explanation: Article 21 deals with the protection of life and personal liberty.
Article 32 allows citizens to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
Article 29 deals with the protection of the interests of minorities.

questions.explanation: Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) allows citizens to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Article 19 deals with the protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc. Article 21 deals with the protection of life and personal liberty. Article 29 deals with the protection of the interests of minorities.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution abolishes 'Untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form?

options.explanation: Article 14 is related to equality before law.
Article 16 is related to equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
Article 17 explicitly abolishes untouchability.
Article 18 is related to abolition of titles.

questions.explanation: Article 17 of the Indian Constitution explicitly abolishes untouchability and makes its practice a punishable offense, thereby upholding the right to equality.

questions.question: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts?

options.explanation: The 24th Amendment Act is related to the amendment of the Constitution.
The 42nd Amendment Act added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.
The 44th Amendment Act is related to the amendment of the Constitution.
The 61st Amendment Act is related to the amendment of the Constitution.

questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976, also known as the 'Mini-Constitution', added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Panchayati Raj System in India was constitutionalized through which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts?

options.explanation: The 61st Amendment Act is related to the reduction of voting age.
The 73rd Amendment Act granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.
The 74th Amendment Act is related to the amendment of the Constitution.
The 86th Amendment Act is related to the amendment of the Constitution.

questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions, making provisions for their establishment and functioning, and added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.

questions.question: What is the minimum age prescribed for a person to be eligible for election as the President of India?

options.explanation: The minimum age for election as a member of the Lok Sabha is 25 years.
The minimum age for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years.
The minimum age for election as the President of India is 35 years.
There is no such requirement for the President of India.

questions.explanation: Article 58 of the Indian Constitution specifies the qualifications for election as President. One of the key requirements is that the person must have completed 35 years of age.

questions.question: A Money Bill can be introduced only in which house of the Indian Parliament?

options.explanation: A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
A Money Bill is not introduced in a joint sitting.

options.text: Either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha
options.explanation: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

questions.explanation: Article 110 of the Indian Constitution defines a Money Bill. It explicitly states that a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and not in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty as enshrined in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To protect and improve the natural environment.
options.explanation: This is a Fundamental Duty.
This is a Fundamental Duty.
Paying taxes is not explicitly listed as a Fundamental Duty.

options.text: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions.
options.explanation: This is a Fundamental Duty.

questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment Act. While paying taxes is a civic responsibility, it is not explicitly listed as a Fundamental Duty in the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: The Chief Election Commissioner of India is appointed by whom?

options.explanation: The Prime Minister does not appoint the Chief Election Commissioner.
The Chief Justice does not appoint the Chief Election Commissioner.
The Parliament does not appoint the Chief Election Commissioner.
The President appoints the Chief Election Commissioner.

questions.explanation: Article 324(2) of the Indian Constitution states that the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners shall be appointed by the President.

questions.question: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 2019 deals with which of the following provisions?

options.text: Implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST).
options.explanation: The GST is implemented through a different act.

options.text: Granting constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).
options.explanation: The NCBC is granted constitutional status through a different act.

options.text: Providing 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in education and public employment.
options.explanation: The 103rd Amendment Act provides 10% reservation for EWS.

options.text: Extending the reservation for SCs and STs in Lok Sabha and state assemblies for another ten years.
options.explanation: The reservation for SCs and STs is extended through a different act.

questions.explanation: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, amended Articles 15 and 16 to provide 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in government jobs and educational institutions.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can a High Court issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose?

options.explanation: Article 32 is related to the Supreme Court's power to issue writs.
Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.
Article 139 is related to the Supreme Court's jurisdiction.
Article 21 is related to the protection of life and personal liberty.

questions.explanation: Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto) not only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights but also for 'any other purpose', making its scope wider than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32, which is limited to Fundamental Rights only.

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains provisions regarding the anti-defection law?

options.explanation: The Seventh Schedule is related to the distribution of powers between the Union and the States.
The Eighth Schedule is related to the recognition of languages.
The Ninth Schedule is related to the validation of certain laws and regulations.
The Tenth Schedule contains provisions regarding the anti-defection law.

questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule was added to the Constitution by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985, commonly known as the Anti-Defection Law. It lays down the process by which legislators may be disqualified on grounds of defection.

questions.question: Which one of the following schedules of the Constitution of India deals with the allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha)?

options.explanation: The Third Schedule is related to forms of oaths.
The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
The Fifth Schedule deals with the administration and control of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes.
The Sixth Schedule deals with the administration of tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.explanation: The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

questions.question: The concept of “Judicial Review” in India is borrowed from the Constitution of:

options.explanation: The concept of Judicial Review in India is not borrowed from the United Kingdom.
The concept of Judicial Review in India is not borrowed from Australia.
The concept of Judicial Review in India is borrowed from the United States of America.
The concept of Judicial Review in India is not borrowed from Canada.

questions.explanation: The concept of Judicial Review in India is borrowed from the United States of America, where the Supreme Court has the power to review and invalidate laws and executive actions that are incompatible with the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for the appointment of the Governor of a State by the President?

options.explanation: Article 153 states that there shall be a Governor for each State.
Article 155 of the Constitution of India provides for the appointment of the Governor of a State by the President.
Article 156 deals with the term of office of the Governor.
Article 158 specifies the qualifications for the appointment of the Governor.

questions.explanation: Article 155 of the Constitution of India provides for the appointment of the Governor of a State by the President.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Panchayati Raj System in India: Statement 1 - The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 provides for a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj. Statement 2 - The Chairperson of a Panchayat at the intermediate level is elected by and from amongst the elected members of the Panchayat. Statement 3 - The State Election Commission is responsible for conducting elections to the Panchayats under the supervision of the Election Commission of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.explanation: Both Statement 1 and Statement 3 are correct.
Statement 2 is incorrect.
Both Statement 1 and Statement 3 are correct.
Statement 2 is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 provides for a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj. Statement 3 is correct: The State Election Commission is responsible for conducting elections to the Panchayats under the supervision of the Election Commission of India.

questions.question: The term 'Judicial Activism' in the context of the Indian judiciary refers to:

options.text: The process of judicial appointments being influenced by political considerations
options.explanation: This is not the definition of Judicial Activism.

options.text: The judiciary's role in interpreting laws strictly without considering societal changes
options.explanation: This is actually the definition of Judicial Restraint.

options.text: The proactive role of the judiciary in addressing issues of public interest and enforcing fundamental rights
options.explanation: Judicial Activism refers to the proactive role of the judiciary in addressing issues of public interest, enforcing fundamental rights, and ensuring justice beyond the traditional scope of litigation.

options.text: The limitation of judicial powers to only constitutional matters
options.explanation: This is the opposite of Judicial Activism.

questions.explanation: Judicial Activism refers to the proactive role of the judiciary in addressing issues of public interest, enforcing fundamental rights, and ensuring justice beyond the traditional scope of litigation.
